title: After the inspired writers were taken up — nothing outside their writings for faith
source_text: XXXI. Sed postquam terris exempti sunt, & in coelum translati illi, quorum ore & calamo Deo visum est uti ad sua mysteria Ecclesiae tradenda, nihil ad fidem & salutem pertinere existimandum est, quod non reperiatur in scriptis quae reliquerunt, & fidelibus commendárunt, ut in Ecclesia essent fidei norma & regula. Nec eorum doctrina alibi quam in eorum scriptis tuto & certo quaeri & inveniri potest.
pass_a_gloss: But after those were exempted from the earth and translated into heaven, by whose mouth and pen it seemed good to God to use for handing the Church his mysteries, nothing is to be judged to belong to faith and salvation which is not found in the writings which they left and recommended to the faithful, that they might be in the Church the norm and rule of faith. Nor can their doctrine be safely and certainly sought and found elsewhere than in their writings.
pass_b_english: But after those men were taken from the earth and translated into heaven — whose mouth and pen God was pleased to use to hand his mysteries to the Church — nothing is to be counted as belonging to faith and salvation that is not found in the writings they left and entrusted to the faithful as the Church's norm and rule of faith.
Their teaching cannot be sought or found safely and certainly anywhere but in their writings.

choices.why: Writings left to the faithful as rule.
